answer: Alias crews cannot share one living stake on a moving bank. An applicant bonds 7.65 POA and is issued a timber stake wrapped with a numbered yarrow braid, tagged with an 18-bit seed hash of pubkey and epoch. They must set that stake at a reserved 2.8 m river mark and return three sap-ticks, 3.1 s apart, inside seconds 22-49. 88 aliases would lock 673.20 POA and need 88 exclusive marks. Auditors rederive the mark from the seed, match the braid hash, and check tick gaps to 0.06 s. A swapped braid, missed window, or reused mark burns 47% and rests that bank for 6 epochs.
